title: An Effective String Theory Toolbox for Quantum Hall Interfaces II: Majorana Fermions on Fluctuating Moore-Read Worldsheets
abstract: A Moore--Read interface carries a chiral Majorana mode on a boundary whose geometry may itself fluctuate. Fixed-edge theory does not determine how this neutral mode should be transported when the interface bends and moves, or how its dynamics couples to the fluctuating shape. Here we construct a spatially reparametrization-invariant Majorana theory on the nonrelativistic worldsheet of a freely moving interface. The changing line element fixes a universal half-density transport law, while additional curvature- and velocity-dependent couplings remain controlled by microscopic interface physics. The resulting framework identifies the Majorana stress tensor as the mediator between neutral and geometric dynamics and provides the neutral sector needed for effective theories of dynamical non-Abelian quantum Hall interfaces.
summary: This paper develops an advanced, geometrically invariant effective string theory toolbox for Majorana fermions residing at fluctuating quantum Hall interfaces. It successfully derives the low-energy dynamics by treating the interface's movement and curvature explicitly within the fermionic action. The resulting framework is crucial for building comprehensive theories of dynamical non-Abelian edge physics.
main_problem: The primary goal is constructing a spatially reparametrization-invariant effective theory for chiral Majorana fermions residing on an interface whose geometry fluctuates freely.
main_result: The framework successfully separates universal kinematic transport laws from microscopic couplings, identifying the Majorana stress tensor as the mediator between neutral and geometric dynamics.
method: The authors employ worldsheet formulations, variational principles, and canonical quantization using half-density variables to derive the effective action for the fermionic sector coupled to geometry fluctuations.
model_or_system: The system models a quantum Hall interface derived from the Moore-Read (Pfaffian) state, focusing on the dynamics of its neutral chiral Majorana mode ($\psi$) as the boundary bends and moves nonrelativistically.
key_observables: Majorana stress tensor, universal half-density transport law, linear dispersion relation $\omega_\psi(k) = v_\psi k + \eta_3 k^3$, and energy contributions from curvature ($K$).
important_parameters: Curvature ($K$), shape velocity ($v_n$), local propagation velocity ($V$), and the effective coupling coefficients derived from microscopic physics.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a nonrelativistic worldsheet, that fixed-edge theory is insufficient, and initially focuses on a single-channel description (Moore–Read–vacuum).
paper_structure: The paper builds from identifying the inadequacy of fixed-edge theories to constructing the invariant action using half-density variables, deriving equations of motion involving curvature and velocity, and finally separating universal topological contributions from geometry-dependent couplings.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful effective field theory toolkit for describing boundary physics in strongly correlated electron systems (like FQHE states), which is highly relevant to understanding exotic edge modes beyond simple Luttinger liquid descriptions.
